subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For a continuous random variable X, which statement is always true?
solution_latex: A single point has zero area under a continuous density, so P(X=x)=0.
common_mistake: A density height can exceed one; probability is an integral.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X is Uniform(a,b), its density on (a,b) is
solution_latex: A constant density over length b−a must have height 1/(b−a).
common_mistake: Normalize by interval length, not endpoint sum.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: The derivative of an absolutely continuous CDF F is
solution_latex: The density satisfies f(x)=F′(x) wherever the derivative exists.
common_mistake: The CDF is accumulated probability, not density.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Which continuous distribution is memoryless?
solution_latex: The exponential survival function satisfies P(X>s+t | X>s)=P(X>t).
common_mistake: Geometric is the discrete memoryless analogue.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X follows N(μ,σ²), then (X−μ)/σ follows
solution_latex: Centering by μ and scaling by the standard deviation produces a standard normal.
common_mistake: Divide by σ, not variance σ².

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: The support of a chi-square random variable is
solution_latex: A chi-square variable is a sum of squared standard normals, hence nonnegative.
common_mistake: It is continuous despite integer degrees of freedom.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Which are properties of every CDF?
options: Limits 0 and 1 at negative and positive infinity
solution_latex: Every CDF has the first three properties. Jumps are allowed, so differentiability is not required.
common_mistake: Discrete CDFs have jumps.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Compared with N(0,1), a Student t distribution has
solution_latex: Student t has heavier tails, reflecting uncertainty from estimating scale.
common_mistake: The t distribution is symmetric on the real line.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For continuous X, P(a<X≤b) equals
solution_latex: CDF increments give interval probability F(b)−F(a).
common_mistake: Use CDF values, not density endpoint heights.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X follows Exp(λ) under the rate parameterization, E[X] is
solution_latex: The mean waiting time is the reciprocal of the event rate.
common_mistake: Some texts parameterize by mean; check the convention.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: A density is f(x)=cx² on 0<x<2. Enter c.
solution_latex: Normalization gives c∫₀²x²dx=c(8/3)=1, hence c=3/8.
common_mistake: Integrate the density over its full support.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X is Uniform(2,8), enter E[X].
solution_latex: The continuous-uniform mean is the midpoint (2+8)/2=5.
common_mistake: Include both endpoints in the midpoint.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X is Uniform(2,8), enter Var(X).
solution_latex: Variance is (b−a)²/12=36/12=3.
common_mistake: Variance uses squared interval length.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X follows Exp(0.5), enter −log P(X>4).
solution_latex: P(X>4)=exp(−0.5·4)=exp(−2), so the negative log is 2.
common_mistake: Use the survival function, not the CDF.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X follows N(10,9), enter the z-score of X=16.
solution_latex: The standard deviation is 3, so z=(16−10)/3=2.
common_mistake: The second normal parameter is variance here.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: A CDF is F(x)=x² on 0≤x≤1. Enter 10P(0.2<X≤0.6).
solution_latex: The probability is 0.36−0.04=0.32; scaling gives 3.2.
common_mistake: Subtract CDF values, not endpoints.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For exponential X, P(X>3)=0.4. Enter 100P(X>6 | X>3).
solution_latex: Memorylessness gives P(X>6 | X>3)=P(X>3)=0.4.
common_mistake: Reset the remaining wait after conditioning.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Three independent standard normals are squared and added. Enter the chi-square degrees of freedom.
solution_latex: The sum of three independent squared standard normals is chi-square with 3 df.
common_mistake: Count the squared independent standard normals.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If X follows N(4,16), enter Var((X−4)/4).
solution_latex: Subtracting 4 changes no variance; dividing by 4 divides variance by 16.
common_mistake: Variance scales by the square.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: A density is f(x)=2x on 0<x<1. Enter its median.
common_mistake: Median splits probability area, not support length.
